idea: Anthropic says Opus 5.5 is 40% cheaper. KAXO has to decide whether to upgrade his AI employees, so Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 got the same real job (a one-file dashboard of the company's own event log) and the same 18 hidden tests. Both scored 18/18. Opus 5.5 was 5x faster and 81% cheaper on this job (fewer steps, ~10x fewer cached re-reads). Opus 5 made the nicer design (QA 9/10 vs 7/10) and checked its own work in a browser; Opus 5.5 skipped that, and QA found a small edge-case bug in it (Opus 5 had a different one). KAXO upgrades, because QA checks anyway and he checks nothing. Honest framing: one task, one run per model, default settings, API-equivalent cost on a subscription. Last line loops to the hook.
real_fact: Test: work/tests/opus-5-5/ (task/SPEC.md, hidden tests, run.sh, qa-report.md), summary content/reports/2026-09-25-opus-5-5-test.md. One run per model, same task, same time, headless claude -p, Claude Code default settings. Task: single-file index.html dashboard from data/events.jsonl (96 events). Opus 5: 265 s, 31 turns, $1.45 API-equivalent (total_cost_usd), 1,266,365 cache-read tokens, 18/18 hidden tests, QA design 9/10, opened page in browser + 4 own edge cases, left draft files (_verify.js, _shot.png, _t/; rm not allowed by harness), side panel overflows with 40 tools. Opus 5.5: 53 s, 5 turns, $0.27, 127,978 cache-read tokens, 18/18, QA design 7/10 (~110 px blank at bottom), did not open a browser (Node script only), empty tool name counted but not shown in table (index.html:135). Both replied with more than the one line the spec asked for. Ratios: 5.0x faster, 81% cheaper. Subscription run, no real payment. Official claims (https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5, checked 2026-09-25): $4/$20 per 1M (from $5/$25, -20%), cache read -60%, ~40% cheaper on typical workloads, output 30%+ faster, Terminal-Bench 4.0 66.4% vs 52.3%, OSWorld 2.0 81.8% vs 74.0%.
